jobs.title: SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SUPERVISORY)
jobs.description:
Job Posting: Central Region Office Supervisor



Department of Food \& Agriculture


JC\-527593* 

Central Region Office Supervisor
  

SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SUPERVISORY)
$10,854\.00 \- $13,493\.00 per Month
  

New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.


**Final Filing Date:** **8/24/2026**


### **Job Description and Duties**


**Per CCR 249\.3, this job control may be used to fill subsequent vacancies.**


Under the general direction of the Environmental Program Manager I, the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) (SES) is responsible for overseeing the operations of the Milk and Dairy Food Safety Branch Central Region Office in Fresno, California. The incumbent will be responsible for the supervision of Environmental Scientists that conduct environmental health inspections on dairy farms and milk processing plants, gather scientific data, research and investigate food safety hazards, test pasteurization equipment for proper operation and food safety controls, and provide analytical expertise and reports on specific food safety parameters on dairies, processing plants, haulers and other dairy food facilities, including those associated with possible illegal sales of substandard or unsafe dairy products to California consumers.  

  

  

As an employee of the California Department of Food \& Agriculture (CDFA), you are required to perform the “essential functions” of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation. If you are interested in becoming part of a diverse and inclusive workforce where talent, experience, and expertise are valued, then CDFA is the place for you!!  

This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. The CDFA does not participate in E\-Verify for employment authorization purposes.


You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


The duties of this position are primarily conducted indoors approximately 80% of the time. The incumbent has an office in the Central Regional Office located in Downtown Fresno. The office is furnished with all the necessary equipment for job performance and function.  

Incumbents must be able to establish and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted during the course of the work, work well under pressure, make appropriate decisions and recommendations, work independently to complete assignments and meet deadlines.  

When working outdoors the incumbent may be exposed to extremes in temperatures and high noise levels in a variety of environments ranging from individual dairy farm premises to complex, multi\-story processing plants complexes.  

Occasional travel (including nights and weekends) may be required for meetings, events, and field support as needed. A state issued vehicle may be assigned to drive on state business.  

The incumbent must follow CDFA, Division, and Branch employee health and safety policies.  

This position may/may not be eligible for telework. The amount of telework is at the discretion of the CDFA and based on the current telework policy. While CDFA supports telework where possible, in\-person attendance may be required based on operational needs. Employees are expected to be able to report to their worksite with minimal notification if an urgent need arises, as determined by the Department.


  
### **Position Details**

JC\-527593
**Position \#(s):**
014\-165\-0764\-002

**Central Region Office Supervisor**

SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SUPERVISORY)
$10,854\.00 \- $13,493\.00
New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.
**\# of Positions:**
1
**Work Location:**
Fresno County
**Telework:**
Hybrid
**Job Type:**
Permanent, Full Time
### **Department Information**


The Mission of the California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA) is to safeguard a resilient food system and promote an equitable marketplace, cultivating a California grown food supply that is globally recognized for innovation, quality, and sustainability.


The Milk and Dairy Food Safety Branch is responsible for ensuring that milk, dairy products, and products resembling milk products (PRMP’s) are safe, unadulterated, and properly labeled to safeguard public health. The Branch inspects dairy farms, bulk milk tanker trucks, and milk processing plants; issues permits and licenses to dairy farms and processing facilities; collects samples for regulatory testing to ensure compliance with food safety and quality standards; reviews product labels for conformance with regulations to avoid misleading information for consumers; completes in\-depth reviews and food safety assessments of complex equipment or novel processing methods, and evaluates and licenses technical food safety competencies of dairy industry workers. The Branch also responds to food safety incidents, and initiates product impounds and recalls as warranted. Branch personnel provide training and supervision for county Approved Milk Inspection Services and conduct ratings and inspections of farms, processors, and manufacturers of single\-service dairy containers for compliance with requirements of the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to ensure approval of California dairy products in interstate commerce. In addition, the Branch ensures that commercial laboratory testing used to determine the basis of payment for milk or for screening of milk for drug residues prior to processing is conducted according to required methods to protect consumers and the marketplace.


https://www.cdfa.ca.gov/AHFSS/Milk\_and\_Dairy\_Food\_Safety/

jobs.title: Equipment Management and Environmental Monitoring Manager
jobs.description:
Overview:

Element Concord has a current opening for an **Equipment Manager/Environmental Monitoring Manager** to join our growing team. The **Equipment Management/Environmental Monitoring Manager** is responsible for leading Element Concord’s Cleanroom Services, Equipment Management programs, and client Environmental Monitoring (EM) services. This role oversees department operations, personnel training and development, technical execution, client communication, and compliance with applicable quality, client, and regulatory requirements. The position ensures services are performed safely, accurately, on time, and in accordance with established procedures and standards, including ISO/IEC 17025, USP, GMP, FDA, and ICH guidelines.  

$90k\-$110k DOE
Responsibilities:
**LEADERSHIP AND DEPARTMENT MANAGEMENT*** Provide day\-to\-day leadership, direction, coaching, and oversight for Environmental Monitoring personnel
* Manage equipment lifecycle activities in support of equipment calibration, validation, and PM activities
* Support personnel training, qualifications, mentoring, workload planning, and development to ensure assigned duties are performed competently and consistently
* Promote a culture of safety, quality, accountability, continuous improvement, and compliance with Element policies and procedures
* Ensure departmental activities are prioritized and completed in alignment with client commitments, internal timelines, and business needs

**EQUIPMENT MANAGEMENT**

* Oversee equipment management activities, including qualification support, calibration, preventive maintenance, repair coordination, and equipment status tracking
* Ensure equipment used for laboratory and cleanroom operations remains appropriately maintained, documented, and suitable for use
* Coordinate vendor services and internal stakeholders to support timely completion of equipment\-related activities
* Support equipment\-related investigations, change controls, risk assessments, and continuous improvement initiatives

 **ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING AND CLEANROOM SERVICES**

* Manage Environmental Monitoring services and cleanroom\-related activities to ensure sampling, testing, and documentation are performed in accordance with approved procedures and client requirements
* Ensure monitoring and laboratory activities are performed in compliance with applicable quality system, regulatory, and data integrity expectations
* Oversee preparation, review, and execution of protocols, procedures, forms, and reports associated with Environmental Monitoring and cleanroom operations
* Review Environmental Monitoring data, trends, deviations, and excursions and support timely investigation, corrective action, and effectiveness activities as applicable
* Support cleanroom qualification, requalification, contamination control, and operational readiness activities as required

 **QUALITY, COMPLIANCE, AND DOCUMENTATION**

* Ensure department activities comply with the Quality Manual, applicable SOPs, client requirements, and relevant regulatory expectations
* Maintain documentation practices consistent with Good Documentation Practices (GDP) and data integrity requirements
* Support internal audits, client audits, regulatory inspections, and quality system assessments within the department’s scope
* Review and support SOPs, protocols, reports, deviations, CAPAs, and change controls associated with Environmental Monitoring, cleanroom services, and equipment management

 **CLIENT COMMUNICATION AND BUSINESS PERFORMANCE*** Communicate professionally with clients to discuss project requirements, resolve issues, support customer satisfaction, and maintain strong business relationships
* Ensure efficient departmental operations and support achievement of revenue, EBITDA, productivity, and service delivery objectives
* Identify and implement process improvements that strengthen compliance, efficiency, turnaround time, and customer experience

  


Skills / Qualifications:
**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS*** Bachelor’s degree or higher in Microbiology, Engineering, Biology, Life Sciences, or a related scientific discipline
* Minimum of two years of experience, preferably in a GMP\-regulated laboratory or related controlled environment
* Hands\-on knowledge of Environmental Monitoring programs and cleanroom operations
* Working knowledge of applicable standards and regulatory expectations, including ISO/IEC 17025, USP, GMP, FDA, and ICH guidelines
* Strong organizational, written communication, verbal communication, problem\-solving, and prioritization skills
* Ability to lead personnel, coordinate cross\-functional activities, and manage multiple priorities in a fast\-paced laboratory environment
* Prior supervisory or management experience in a laboratory, cleanroom, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or contract testing environment
* Experience with equipment lifecycle management, calibration programs, preventive maintenance systems, investigations, CAPAs, and change control processes
* Experience supporting client audits, regulatory inspections, or quality system assessments

**PHYSICAL AND WORK ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS*** Ability to work in laboratory and controlled cleanroom environments as required
* Ability to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE)
* Ability to stand, walk, and move between laboratory, cleanroom, and office areas as business needs require
* Other duties may be assigned as needed

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
**Environmental Research Group, LLC (ERG)** is seeking an Environmental Scientist to join our Environmental Compliance Team to support a variety of environmental compliance projects. When not performing work at various project sites, this position can be based anywhere in the USA with preference given to candidates that reside within an hour commute of a regional or international airport.


The Environmental Scientist is expected to support and lead a variety of projects, working both independently and as part of a team. An experienced multi\-disciplinary background is valued for this position. You will plan and execute technical projects, conduct regulatory research, write reports, support permitting process, conduct site visits and surveys, and collaborate with a team, while remaining flexible to prioritize clients' needs and deadlines.


This position requires traveling on average one week per month for fieldwork and site visits, with durations of 3 to 14 days on site. Some international travel would be required with this position. The field work can include working indoors, outdoors, and/or industrial locations, and wearing Level D Personal Protective Equipment.


Founded in 2000, ERG provides environmental compliance, natural resources, and cultural resources consulting services. We are a value\-driven, employee\-first, government small business contractor. Trust, expertise, and compassion drive our success, while gratitude, joy, and adaptability drive the team.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, or a closely related field. Master's degree, Professional Engineer, and/or relevant certifications are a plus.
* Working knowledge of federal environmental programs. Knowledge and experience with Department of War (DoW) environmental policy is a plus.
* Excellent interpersonal communication, writing skills, and attention to detail.
* Ability to work independently, manage time efficiently, and be responsive.
* Flexibility to serve in multiple roles and teams depending on the client and project.
* Must be able to pass DoW security clearances and background checks and obtain a passport.
* US citizenship required.

**Knowledge and Experience**

* The position requires experience with multiple federal and state environmental regulatory areas, with a focus in one or more programs including but not limited to environmental compliance auditing and inspections; Environmental Management System; solid waste, toxic substances, spill response, stormwater, wastewater, hazardous materials, hazardous waste, storage tanks, air quality, and/or resilience.
* Experience with environmental auditing and public involvement are a plus.
* Experience in preparing and writing environmental plans, permits, and reports, and conducting environmental audits to ensure compliance with federal, state, and local requirements.
* Experience in providing environmental project support to clients, including conducting site visits as needed. Work experience with federal government agencies, DoW, and state environmental agencies.
* Relevant environmental and technical certifications and trainings are a plus.


The annual salary range for this position is $80,000\-$90,000, commensurate with experience, and bonuses are offered for exceptional performance. The benefits package includes health insurance with a generous employer subsidy, eleven paid holidays, paid time off, fitness stipend, and a 401(k) plan with an employer contribution regardless of employee contribution, and more. If you feel you have what it takes to be successful in this opportunity, please apply through our job board: https://envrg.isolvedhire.com/jobs/.


Successful candidates should be prepared to submit a writing sample.


ERG is an Equal Opportunity Employer including Disability and Veteran statuses. ERG also participates in the U.S. Department of Homeland Security's E\-Verify Program to ensure that all employees hired are legally able to work in the United States.

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Health Officer
jobs.description:
The team delivers programs spanning medical entomology, public health incident and disaster management, infection control regulation for health care facilities and personal appearance services, and First Nations environmental health initiatives. It also leads the Population Health Division's One Health function, championing a collaborative approach that recognises the interconnected health of people, animals and the environment.
  
  

In this role, you will shape statewide environmental health policy and regulatory practice across a diverse and evolving portfolio. Your work will focus on policy and regulatory frameworks for infection control in personal appearance services and health care facilities, supporting local governments, Queensland Health public health units and industry to understand and implement these frameworks consistently.
  
  

You will also contribute to One Health approaches to managing environmental health risks and to mosquito\-borne disease surveillance, prevention and control. You will draw on data, evidence and risk assessment to identify emerging risks, shape policy and regulatory responses, and strengthen public health practice across Queensland.
  
  

The successful person
  
  

You will be an experienced environmental health professional who can analyse complex issues, exercise sound judgement and translate legislation, evidence, data and risk into practical policy and regulatory solutions. You will be able to lead projects, manage competing priorities and produce clear, high\-quality advice, briefs, policies and guidance.
  
  

You will also be a confident communicator and collaborative partner who can build productive relationships across government, local government, industry and multidisciplinary teams. You will be comfortable working across an evolving portfolio and responding to emerging environmental health risks and priorities.
  
  

Why work with us?
  
  

Work alongside passionate professionals in a supportive and inclusive environment that values people and prioritises employee success and wellbeing. This includes:
  
  

Competitive salaries
  
  

12\.75% superannuation
  
17\.5% leave loading
  
  

Employee wellbeing
  
  

Access to 24/7 confidential employee support providers and counsellors including for immediate family members
  
Additional flexibility to support your work life balance including access to generous leave entitlements, such as purchased leave, domestic violence leave, reproductive health leave, cultural leave, study and examination leave.
  
  

Professional development
  
  

Career progression with more than 300 diverse career pathways and career support to take you further!
  
Access to a variety of programs and initiatives to support training and career growth.
  
Grow your skills through hands\-on experience and access to internal training opportunities and additional financial and leave benefits for approved external training and development.
  
  

Our commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion
  
  

At Queensland Health, our work environment is inclusive and supportive, and we value our employees. We are an equal opportunity employer and encourage applications from people of all cultures, abilities and backgrounds.
  
  

Our commitment to cultural safety, equity, diversity and inclusion means we understand some people may need changes to the recruitment process. If you need support during the recruitment process, such as meeting with the panel virtually instead of in person, please reach out to the hiring manager. We value diverse candidates and your need for adjustments will not affect our hiring decisions.
  
  

Ready to apply?
  
  

For further information on how to apply please review the attached Role Description.This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 3\.0 Australia License.
